findings.prior_risk: Weekly scheduled workflow had contents:write and committed harvested JSON/A2A corpus directly to main.
findings.change: Retain scheduled public research ingestion and validation, remove write permission and git push, upload generated files as a 30-day artifact.
findings.side_effects: Public arXiv GET requests only; no repository mutation.

findings.prior_risk: Weekly schedule invoked every registered WebMCP tool execute({}) in Playwright, then committed logs; push-conflict path performed git pull --no-rebase followed by push.
findings.change: Remove schedule, require manual confirm_live_execution=YES, contents:read, checkout credentials disabled, artifact-only log.
findings.side_effects: Tool invocation can still call external APIs; now manual-only with explicit per-run approval.

findings.prior_risk: Local simulations and artifact generation requested contents:write despite no repository push step.
findings.change: Downgrade to contents:read and persist-credentials:false; retain push/schedule/manual triggers and artifact output.
findings.side_effects: Local simulation and artifact upload only.

findings.prior_risk: Weekly local audit and benchmark summaries committed multiple JSON/JSONL files to main with git push and pull/rebase fallback.
findings.change: Read-only checkout and workflow artifact output; remove commit and push.
findings.side_effects: Local analysis only; audit script explicitly passes github_token=None and github_repo=None.

findings.prior_risk: workflow_run plus weekly schedule used contents:write, injected GITHUB_TOKEN, and pushed GitHub/NPM search results to main.
findings.change: Keep scheduled/public GET enrichment, remove GITHUB_TOKEN secret and repository write, upload results as artifact.
findings.side_effects: Unauthenticated GitHub/NPM search may rate-limit; script already records errors; no repository mutation.

findings.prior_risk: Scheduled check minted a GitHub App installation access token via POST even though the script only checked the response; Databricks SQL used a hard-coded SELECT 1 but token scope was unknown.
findings.change: Add contents:read and persist-credentials:false; change GitHub App check to GET installation metadata, avoiding token minting.
findings.side_effects: Databricks SQL SELECT 1 remains a POST API call; read-only intent is explicit but actual token scope is not verifiable from repository evidence.

findings.prior_risk: Daily schedule authenticated to Kaggle and intended to download/train/submit up to five baseline competition entries without per-run approval. Workflow command referenced a nonexistent root script; actual script is under scripts/.
findings.change: Remove schedule; require confirm_external_submission=YES and exact comma-separated competition slug allowlist; contents:read; correct script path; both script copies refuse before authentication when allowlist is empty.
findings.side_effects: A manually approved run can still submit to exact allowlisted Kaggle competitions. No data/submission files are uploaded as artifacts.

tests_added: Kaggle submission requires per-run YES and exact competition allowlist.
Scheduled public research jobs write workflow artifacts rather than main.
WebMCP live sandbox requires manual approval.
Hover Bike simulation uses read-only repository access.
Pillars check uses a read-only GitHub installation lookup.
Duplicate Kaggle runner copy also refuses before authentication without allowlist.
residual_risks: The changes are only on PR #1623; all corresponding workflows remain active on main until approved merge.
Databricks token scope for the scheduled SELECT 1 check is not observable from repository code; verify it is a dedicated read-only SQL token.
Other manual-only workflows with write permissions and release/tag-triggered workflows require a separate review.
No full workflow inventory has yet been exhaustively classified by trigger, permission, external side effect and secret scope.
Root requirements.tx appears unreferenced in inspected build/docs/workflows; no lockfiles exist; CI installs only a subset of app dependencies.
next_actions: Run exact-head CI and fail-closed gate after all changes.
Inspect job logs to verify the new tests were collected and passed.
Audit remaining manual workflows and tag-triggered release actions.
Confirm Databricks token is restricted to read-only SQL warehouse use.
Keep main untouched and do not merge without explicit approval.
